description: We’re a student-led team from North Macedonia with a shared interest in physics, spaceflight, and game development. For Project Exodus, we bring together mission design, Unreal Engine development, 3D art, and sound design. We’re building a game that lets players learn how satellite missions work by making the decisions themselves.
summary:
Project Exodus is an educational spaceflight game about planning and carrying out satellite missions around Earth. From preparing a rocket for launch to collecting and transmitting data from orbit, players make engineering decisions with limited resources. The choices they make before liftoff shape what their satellite can accomplish once it reaches orbit.

By following a mission from preparation to operation, players see how launch, orbit, and spacecraft design work together. The goal is to help students understand the trade-offs behind real space missions by letting them make those decisions for themselves.
details:
In Project Exodus, players work toward a mission objective by preparing a rocket, making decisions about the spacecraft and its instruments, and carrying out operations in Earth orbit. During an Earth observation mission, for example, a satellite can run out of storage before it finishes surveying an area. The player then has to transmit the data already collected before continuing the survey.

We designed the game to connect decisions made on the ground with their consequences in orbit. The instrument a player chooses affects what the satellite can observe, how much power it needs, and how much data it has to send back. Our aim is to give students a hands-on way to explore the trade-offs behind real spacecraft missions and see how those choices affect the outcome.

We are developing the PC game in Unreal Engine 4.27 using Blueprints and creating 3D assets in Blender. We used published rocket specifications as references for the vehicle models and simplified the simulation so players can focus on the decisions that matter to each mission.
